cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women who experienced late-onset pregnancy complications, had a low risk for chromosomal abnormalities, and absence of fetal abnormalities, and 100 women with uneventful pregnancies as controls.
finding: Patients with late-onset pregnancy complications had a significantly higher prevalence of antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) compared to controls (31% vs 10%), and aPL-positive patients had a significantly higher risk of preterm birth.
